<h1 id="Drug-Repurposing-&amp;-Knowledge-Graphs-%E2%80%94-Fajgenbaum-Lab-(Track-3)">Drug Repurposing &amp; Knowledge Graphs — Fajgenbaum Lab (Track 3)<a class="anchor-link" href="#Drug-Repurposing-&amp;-Knowledge-Graphs-%E2%80%94-Fajgenbaum-Lab-(Track-3)">¶</a></h1><p>This notebook walks <strong>Track 3</strong> from NMF-based drug repositioning (repoDB-scale

<p><strong>Narrative:</strong> Start from nonnegative factorization of a sparse drug–disease matrix
(repoDB-motivated pipelines), narrow to pharmacophenomic <strong>pathway activation</strong>
and drug–pathway alignment (mTOR ↔ sirolimus), then broaden to <strong>TransE</strong>
embeddings over a synthetic biomedical KG (drugs, diseases, genes, pathways).</p>
<p><strong>Rust binaries (wetSpring checkout):</strong> <code>validate_nmf_drug_repurposing</code>,
<code>validate_fajgenbaum_pathway</code>, <code>validate_knowledge_graph_embedding</code>
(e.g. <code>cargo run --release --bin validate_nmf_drug_repurposing</code> from <code>barracuda/</code>).</p>

<h2 id="NMF-drug%E2%80%93disease-matrix-factorization-(Lee-&amp;-Seung)">NMF drug–disease matrix factorization (Lee &amp; Seung)<a class="anchor-link" href="#NMF-drug%E2%80%93disease-matrix-factorization-(Lee-&amp;-Seung)">¶</a></h2><p><strong>Nonnegative matrix factorization</strong> approximates a nonnegative association matrix
(V \in \mathbb{R}<em>+^{n \times m}) as (V \approx W H) with
(W \in \mathbb{R}</em>+^{n \times k}), (H \in \mathbb{R}_+^{k \times m}), using
multiplicative updates (Gao/Yang-style repoDB pipelines use the same family of
models at full scale).</p>
<p>For this notebook we use a <strong>synthetic</strong> (50 \times 30) matrix with clear
block structure (<strong>10 drug clusters</strong> × <strong>3 disease groups</strong>) and <strong><code>k = 8</code></strong>
latent factors—small enough to run interactively while mirroring sparse
repoDB-shaped problems.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<h2 id="Fajgenbaum-pathway-scoring-(JCI-2019)">Fajgenbaum pathway scoring (JCI 2019)<a class="anchor-link" href="#Fajgenbaum-pathway-scoring-(JCI-2019)">¶</a></h2><p>Published <strong>pathway activation scores</strong> (proteomics) drive a simple
<strong>drug–pathway match</strong>: each drug is mapped to its primary target pathway; the
top pathway is <strong>PI3K/AKT/mTOR</strong>, consistent with <strong>sirolimus</strong> (mTOR inhibitor)
as the mechanistic match in IL-6-blockade-refractory iMCD.</p>
<p><strong>Selectivity</strong> is illustrated with <strong>cosine similarity</strong> between each drug’s
pathway indicator (weighted by activation on that pathway) and the global
activation profile over pathways.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<h2 id="TransE-knowledge-graph-embedding">TransE knowledge-graph embedding<a class="anchor-link" href="#TransE-knowledge-graph-embedding">¶</a></h2><p><strong>TransE:</strong> ( \mathbf{h} + \mathbf{r} \approx \mathbf{t} ).
Energy (|\mathbf{h} + \mathbf{r} - \mathbf{t}|); conventionally <strong>score</strong>
(= -|\mathbf{h} + \mathbf{r} - \mathbf{t}|)/ margin ranking on corrupted triples.</p>
<p>We train on a <strong>synthetic biomedical KG</strong>: cluster-structured triples for
<code>treats</code>, <code>targets</code>, <code>associated_with</code>, and <code>part_of</code>, then report <strong>mean rank</strong>
(lower is better, filtered) and <strong>Hits@10</strong> on a held-out triple set.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
